hero.angle: Port St. Lucie SWAT arrests 48-year-old Virgil Jason Vinz on five counts of sexual activity with a minor after early-morning warrant; detail charges, arrest circumstances, and his prior 2023 conviction and probation violation history as case remains active.

hero.body:
Port St. Lucie police arrested a 48-year-old man Thursday morning on five counts of sexual activity with a minor and six counts of contributing to the delinquency or dependency of a child after a SWAT team executed a search warrant at a home in the 900 block of Southwest Jaslo Avenue. Officers took Virgil Jason Vinz into custody without incident around 6 a.m.

Neighbors reported hearing loud booms before seeing officers outside the home. Police spokesperson Brandon Martinez said the sounds were Noise Flash Diversionary Devices used during the SWAT team's entry, not gunshots. Martinez said officers use the devices during high-risk operations for the safety of both officers and the individual inside.

Vinz faces five second-degree felony charges and six first-degree misdemeanor charges. Court records show he pleaded no contest and was adjudicated guilty in 2023 on charges of battery on a law enforcement officer and contributing to the delinquency of a child. He later violated probation before completing Mental Health Court in October 2024.

Martinez said police take cases involving children very seriously but are limited in what they can discuss while the case remains active. Authorities have not said what evidence was recovered from the home or what prompted the investigation. Vinz remained in the St. Lucie County Jail as of Thursday night with bond pending.

When conducting a high-risk operation, these are utilized just for the safety of both the officers and the individual," Martinez said. Authorities have not said what evidence was recovered from the home or what prompted the investigation and say they are limited in what they can discuss while the case remains active.

Court records show Vinz pleaded no contest and was adjudicated guilty in 2023 on charges of battery on a law enforcement officer and contributing to the delinquency of a child. Records also show he later violated probation before completing Mental Health Court in October 2024. Martinez said officers are familiar with Vinz from previous encounters but emphasized the current case is separate from any prior incidents.

Vinz remained in the St. Lucie County Jail as of Thursday night, with bond pending. "As a father of three myself, we take it very serious anytime there is a child involved," Martinez said.

cards.body:
Three St. Lucie County firefighters terminated following an investigation into alleged hazing incidents publicly challenged the fairness of the probe at a Wednesday fire district meeting, with the dispute now moving to arbitration. The firefighters were among five disciplined after videos surfaced that appeared to show them administering electric shocks to newer employees. Jordon Hutchinson, one of the terminated firefighters, said the former employees are calling the disciplinary action retaliation for filing complaints against district leadership.

Community members at the meeting urged the district to reinstate the firefighters, alleging the investigation was limited and mischaracterized. Residents argued that some allegations were reviewed internally while others were handled by independent investigators. The board voted 4-1 against a motion to suspend the district chief and attorney.

"We were held accountable. They need to be held accountable," Hutchinson said. "Even after being fired, we're still here today trying to fix the process." The fire district disciplined five firefighters total following the independent investigation into the hazing incidents.

cards.teaser: Three firefighters fired after videos showed them administering electric shocks to newer employees are calling the investigation limited and retaliatory. The fire district board voted 4-1 against suspending the district chief and attorney.

hero.body:
Fort Pierce police have formally charged 28-year-old Cornelius Trevon Ivory with first-degree murder in connection with a July 5 shooting on South 14th Street that killed a 28-year-old man. The Fort Pierce Police Department announced Ivory was identified as the suspect through an extensive investigation that included eyewitness accounts, information from community members, law enforcement databases and assistance from the Palm Bay Police Department. Authorities served Ivory with the murder arrest warrant while he was already in the St. Lucie County Jail on an unrelated weapons charge from July 24. Ivory faces charges of first-degree murder, attempted first-degree murder, possession of a firearm and possession of a firearm by a convicted felon.

The shooting occurred after the victims were involved in an earlier altercation at the 5800 block of Okeechobee Road before returning to their residence. As the victims arrived home, a man not believed to be involved in the altercation on Okeechobee Road approached them and fired a weapon before leaving the area. A 28-year-old woman sustained a non-life-threatening injury to her hand, while the 28-year-old man sustained multiple gunshot wounds and was transported to a local hospital. The Fort Pierce Police Department announced on July 7 that the man died from his injuries.

Detectives said they developed probable cause for Ivory's arrest through the investigation. Fort Pierce Police obtained an arrest warrant charging Ivory in connection with the killing. Authorities said Ivory was already being held at the St. Lucie County Jail involving possession of weapon by a convicted felon on July 24 when he was served with the murder warrant.

Ivory remains in the St. Lucie County Jail, and his first appearance in the murder case was Friday. Investigators credited members of the public who came forward with information during the case, as well as the Palm Bay Police Department for assisting in the investigation. The investigation remains active. Anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.

Detectives said they developed probable cause for Ivory's arrest through the investigation. Fort Pierce Police obtained an arrest warrant charging Ivory in connection with the killing. Authorities said Ivory was already being held at the St. Lucie County Jail involving possession of weapon by a convicted felon on July 24 when he was served with the murder warrant.

Ivory remains in the St. Lucie County Jail, and his first appearance in the murder case was Friday. Investigators credited members of the public who came forward with information during the case, as well as the Palm Bay Police Department for assisting in the investigation. The investigation remains active. Anyone with additional information is encouraged to contact the Fort Pierce Police Department.
